title: The Sweet on the Wind

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: The sweet on a man's breath comes from somewhere. The yard asks the wind, and the wind asks the pot, and the pot keeps its own counsel. What is carried out is carried out; nothing in the yard is entered.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the Vail kiln-house, in the middle days of Ember

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a one-hundred-and-eighty-six-to-one-hundred-and-eighty-eight-day-old body carried everywhere and told by nobody --- six months and six days to six months and eight days, no roof with a word for it. The surgeon's register colours the noticing (the kiln and the carried fire as counts kept behind a wall with a gap and no payer, a carrying arm as a record in muscle that remembers weight and not cost, the private file turned out as instruments laid on a towel, a hand carried past at two paces read as a body with lead in it, likenesses taken down one at a time before they can stand up and call themselves a rule) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line --- the old life stays offstage --- and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector or back-room interior, no market, no Cross and no Account-day in these days, no Berr, Hessa, soft-cuffed clerk, green-mouthed woman or foundling, no seventh hearing, no tenth stopping, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause, no calling of the loan, no payer named, no private record read and no ending

scenes.title: The Middle Days
scenes.synopsis: First entry, first dated heading and drop capital: Day 186, Ember 7, Seventhday, before first grey through the opening of the kiln, at the bed, the hearth, the loaf shelf's low angle, the kiln mouth and the edge of the Clay Yard. No recap of the close of Chapter 44. The boy is one hundred and eighty-six days old and six months and six days and nobody under any roof says so (T071/T072). The first smell is hot clay under tallow and wet wool with the sour mineral breath of the unswept corner; the first sound is the kiln's breath in fours with a gap, not a bell. Under the floor the carried fire answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and eighty-six days (T088); through the finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings and never invented to stand up as a seventh; overhead the boards keep four nails, four, and a knot the width of a thumb --- three counts in three places that do not become one (T061/T082). The crust lies stiff and leathery two inches from his ear with its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread of drool is frozen and unwiped; his hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the note of water and comes down against the fold. Sella gives every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, says the house where another woman would say I, keeps her half-pace, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and shuts her hand half over nothing without touching it, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale off the coals, and sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, her hand resting a half-beat longer at the setting (T058/T079). The widow's mark hangs where it hung, untouched, because a morning and a shelf are not openings and the one opening was before the kiln on Ember 1. The yard goes around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the pan's gone round place, the bare dark trough whose water is called weather and the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15, with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). The month's danger keeps an order and no name that cannot be carried into a chart: hot clay under tallow, fine grey slate dust ground small as meal, the sweetish edge of lead glaze on a wrong wind off High Kiln, and a rack-worker's pot set down wrong giving its high thin note before its time, which the woman who set it down does not hear; the boy turns toward the note and gets no further, filing it as a danger and not promoting it into a fourth near-full answer, no pot lost and no lesson made (T077, T061/T082). Tarn takes the broom only after it has been given its instruction and tells the kindling Six counted. The next I don't count, six where the house can check and the seventh held where it cannot, says Yes, house to an early thaw and a late while wanting the late because it puts off the paying, sweeps the collector's road without turning, and no collector comes (T036/T076). In the wheel-shed Jorra works with slip dried to the colour of old bone up both forearms, speaks to the wheel before anyone, tells a pot You'll do, knows its full note three turns ahead and withholds it from a High Kiln kiln-master come up on the wrong wind with the sweetish lead edge at one mouth-corner who says a pot singing before its time generally sings itself out early; when Sella's sentence hangs unfinished his bent finger stands in the cold iron until the words reach the pot, a remembered holding and not a new change (T035/T031, T062, T065/T095). Close on his wanting the crust, the breast, the pot handle and a number spoken by somebody who would have known what a number counted, and getting none: his hand comes down against the fold with one hundred and eighty-six exact and unspent.

scenes.title: What Is Remembered Is Not Done Again
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 186, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the kindling, the hearth, the bed and the clay road at the going of the light. The afternoon thins without ending; hot clay lies under tallow and wet wool under that, and below both the sour mineral breath of the Ash corner nobody has swept in two years. Sella stands with her back to the basket at the loaf shelf and moves her lips along a row standing with two unnamed gaps, gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze without touching it, and keeps her finger from beneath the front edge, so the charcoal tally stays unread, uncounted and uncopied and the Day 166 held beat stays where it was left (T100). At the kindling the small knife lies at the very edge of its sill where a man could check it, six years in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it, Ash worked into the creases of Tarn's knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line and no scrubbing lifting it, the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holding what light there is and giving it back. The breath from Seed 16 stands unspent at the top of every reach with its small interval where a breath should have gone in and had not; the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it comes to his teeth and stops short of the word that would call the loan, no figure, no name, no tenth standing up before the seventh year is earned, the nine stoppings still nine objects with no payer named to any, the loan uncalled, the seventh year nearer its end than it has ever stood and not given (T036/T076, T061/T082). The warm stone lies back in its clay pot in the loft above the shed, two days gone and cold, unreconciled by not trying, which is not forgiving; from below the boy files the remembered holding as a remembering and not a holding made again, and does not stand it up with the Day 161 damper fraction, the Day 166 shelf beat or the Day 171 flagstone half-check (T006 held). Sella, within hearing, gives the end of her instruction to the pot and asks nothing; Jorra does not ask about the ear and Tarn does not ask about the room, and the two silences stay unjoined. At the going of the light she carries him home up the clay road, woodsmoke going before her in long low bars and the river wind coming behind with the taste of water over water, going wide around the pan's gone place, the bare dark trough, the rack space with its broken birth-slates and the empty place in the returning line, with a look that asks for nothing and finds nothing, a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098). Under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face, leaves the thread frozen, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed, tells the carried fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale off the coals, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, and does not touch the widow's mark, because a dusk and a bed are not openings and the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour; the two rooms do not touch (T058/T079). In the small hours he turns out the file as instruments laid on a towel: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth from a person and no seventh invented, three near-full answers advanced and unpaid, nine stoppings as objects and not a rule with no tenth, three held changes on three separate places, the loft-sill sound on a fourth place of its own, the two shut-room tellings with no third, the told bell beside the heard, the told figure beside the paid, and the shelf's two gaps, the fold's crust and its gap, the pan's gone round ring and the field's empty place on trays that do not touch, with no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause and no finger drawing the line (T061/T082, T060/T086, T065/T095, T097 held). Close with cold at cheek, temple and the small bare joint at the wrist where the wool rides back, the afterdrop waiting, and one hundred and eighty-six exact, complete and unspent in the dark of the wool.

scenes.title: The Pale Line at the Gum
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated heading: Day 187, Ember 8, Eighthday, before first grey into the morning at the well, the drying racks, the wheel-shed edge, the kiln mouth and the yard's edge of light. The boy is one hundred and eighty-seven days old and six months and seven days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the fire's fifth is still missing under the floor with its payer unnamed for a hundred and eighty-seven days (T088); the river's note and the boards' four nails, four and a knot keep the other two counts in their places (T061/T082). Three or four unnamed men go low into the finger's-width-open back room before first grey and get no name; Sella carries past at the half-pace, turns no head, gives the house no name for them and does not say the room is cold; the two tellings of a counting room shut in the war stand side by side with no third (T035/T031, T065/T095). Jorra comes through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent little finger and under the nails, white in the creases where a fist opened, not bone-coloured slip; he keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray, speaks to the wheel before anyone, tells a pot You'll do, knows its full note and withholds the knowing from a High Kiln kiln-master on the wrong wind with the sweetish lead edge at one mouth-corner, and when Sella's voice goes low and unfinished his bent finger goes to the cold iron and waits while the sentence reaches the pot, a remembered holding and not a new change (T061/T082, T062). A glaze-room hand come up from High Kiln waits at the yard well with the sweetish edge of lead glaze on his breath; when he drinks, the pale line shows at his gum, and he keeps one hand curled at his side rather than using it. The boy reads the body exactly from two paces --- the line at the gum, the held hand, the colour under the nails, the way the man breathes --- in the surgeon's register, and cannot reach any of it or speak any of it; he files it where a danger of the month goes, not among the hearings, not a seventh, not a fourth near-full answer, no name, no figure, no cause and no payer (T077, T061/T082). The yard goes around the two unswept lines called the thaw, the rack space, the pan's gone place and the field's empty place with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098). A neighbour with a wet pot asks what the firing costs; Sella glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze, shuts her hand half over nothing without touching it, and sends the question to the pot and the weather with Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there. The house has said it, and the woman carries it away level with nothing priced, refused or entered (T077, T058/T079). Tarn takes the broom only after its instruction, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, agrees with an early thaw and a late while wanting the late because it puts off the paying, and his stroke goes over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check, so the Day 171 movement is not repeated (T036/T076). Close on the sweet breath passing over the basket and going on up the yard, with the boy's hand going up an inch toward the note of water and coming down against the fold, one hundred and eighty-seven exact and unspent.

scenes.title: A Body Read at Two Paces
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 187, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the kindling, the hearth, the bed and the clay road at the going of the light. The afternoon keeps its order without a name; hot clay under tallow, dry dust and the sweet edge riding the wrong wind gather and are not paid. Sella stands with her back to the basket at the loaf shelf, moves her lips along a row with two unnamed gaps, gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze without touching it, and keeps her finger from beneath the front edge; the charcoal stays unread and the Day 166 held beat stays where it was left (T100). At the kindling the knife is back on the sill at the edge where it can be checked, six counted and the seventh held, the Seed 16 breath unspent with its small interval, Ash worked into the knuckle creases, the clip-ring holding what light there is; the ear-sentence comes to the threshold of the word that would call the loan and stops with no figure and no name, the breath drawn and not spent, the nine stoppings still nine, no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the loan uncalled (T036/T076, T061/T082). The stone in its unmarked pot in the loft stays cold and unreconciled; the boy keeps the remembering on its own place and does not make it a holding done again (T006 held). In the wheel-shed Jorra keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray, gives the men in the back room no name, tells a pot You'll do, keeps his knowing from the men on the wrong wind and holds his bent finger in the cold iron while Sella's unfinished sentence reaches the pot; the two silences stay unjoined and the promise of the foundling's name stays ungiven (T035/T031, T062, T065/T095). At the going of the light Sella carries him home up the clay road, woodsmoke before and river wind behind, going wide around the pan's gone place, the bare dark trough, the rack space and the field's empty place with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098). Under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face, leaves the thread frozen, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting, tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and does not look toward the bed or touch the mark; the two rooms do not touch (T058/T079). In the small hours the boy lays out the file and adds the pale line at the gum as a reading of a body held on a place of its own --- a danger read exactly, worth nothing at two paces, not entered among the six hearings, not a seventh, not one of the three near-full answers, not a stopping, not one of the three held changes and not a fourth likeness stood up to call itself a cause, for a rule is an account that has found a payer (T061/T082, T077). Close with the three counts in three places that do not become one, cold stopped at cheek, temple and wrist, one hundred and eighty-seven exact and unspent, and his hand coming down against the fold.

scenes.title: Carried Out
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated heading: Day 188, Ember 9, Ninthday, before first grey through the carrying-out at midday, at the well, the drying racks, the kiln mouth, the flagstones and the yard's edge. The boy is one hundred and eighty-eight days old and six months and eight days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the fire's fifth is still missing under the floor with its payer unnamed for a hundred and eighty-eight days (T088). THE CHAPTER'S ONE MEANINGFUL CHANGE, PAID SMALL AND NON-FATALLY: the sweetish edge of lead glaze rides a wrong wind off High Kiln; a rack-worker sets a pot down wrong and the pot gives its high thin note before its time and then sings itself out early, and the woman goes on with her hands and makes no lesson of it (T077, T061/T082). Then two men carry the glaze-room hand out of the kiln and across the yard toward the clay road, one with a thumb hooked under the man's arm to keep the head from lopping, the other holding the feet; the man is alive and breathing, the sweet-sickness on his breath, the pale line at his gum, his own hand held limp with the fingers gone the colour of old rope and the nails pewter-pale. Sella sets the basket down at the yard's edge, turns the boy's face as she would turn a pot so the light fell where she wanted it, and goes wide around the space the carriers crossed with a look that asks for nothing and finds nothing, a wide step and no number, giving no instruction to the basket (T058/T079). The boy reads the carried body exactly --- the line at the gum, the sweet breath, the way the hand is held, the thumb under the arm, the colour of the nail beds --- as a man with lead in him, in the surgeon's register, and cannot reach any of it or speak any of it; he is the only adult in the yard and the least use in it. Nobody calls a collector, nobody gives a figure, nobody says what ailed him or makes a lesson of the glaze; the question of a cost goes to the pot and the weather and arrives nowhere, and the cost stays entered in no slate (T077). The yard goes back to its work around the place where the man was carried and around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space, the pan's gone ring and the field's empty place, with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098). No major character dies, no thread is closed, no payer is named, no doctrine stands up and no second edge is owed. Close on the carried man's hand coming up once and going down as the two men go out of the yard with him toward the clay road, while the boy's own hand goes up an inch toward the note of water and comes down against the fold, one hundred and eighty-eight exact and unspent.

scenes.title: Nothing Entered
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 188, Ember 9, Ninthday, afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the kindling, the hearth, the bed and the clay road at the going of the light. The afternoon thins without ending; hot clay lies under tallow and wet wool under that, and below both the sour mineral breath of the unswept corner. Nothing in the yard has been entered for the man carried out: no figure, no slate, no collector, no lesson, no payer named to the keeping (T077). The pot that sang itself out early is swept around, not made an omen, and the dust, the wrong wind and the dust ground small as meal go on spoken of without a second edge paid (T061/T082). Sella stands with her back to the basket at the loaf shelf, moves her lips along a row standing with two unnamed gaps, gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze without touching it, and keeps her finger from beneath the front edge, so the charcoal stays unread and the Day 166 held beat stays where it was left (T100). At the kindling Tarn's knife lies on the sill at the edge where it can be checked, six in the worn thumb-mark where the house can verify them and the seventh at the lip where no thumb has gone, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it, Ash in the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line, the pale clip-ring holding what light there is, the Seed 16 breath unspent with its small interval; the ear-sentence comes to the threshold and stops with no figure and no name, the breath drawn and not spent, the nine stoppings still nine objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the loan uncalled and the seventh year nearer its end than it has ever stood and not given (T036/T076). The stone lies back in its pot in the loft, cold and unreconciled by not trying, which is not forgiving; the boy files the remembering as a remembering and not a holding made again (T006 held). In the wheel-shed Jorra keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray, tells a pot You'll do, withholds the knowing from the men on the wrong wind, gives them no name, and holds his bent finger in the cold iron until Sella's unfinished sentence reaches the pot, the fraction held and unspoken and not a change made twice over; the two shut-room tellings stay two with no third (T035/T031, T062, T065/T095). At the going of the light she carries him home up the clay road, woodsmoke going before her in long low bars and the river wind coming up behind with the taste of water over water, going wide around the pan's gone place, the bare dark trough, the rack space with its broken birth-slates and the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15, with a look and a wide step and no number and no explanation to the basket (T009/T013/T092, T098). Under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, base first and the weight settled the way a woman sets a vessel that must not rock, puts the fold right at his ear and under his chin without once looking at his face, leaves the thread of drool frozen and unwiped, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed, tells the carried fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale off the coals, sets the pot rim out with its handle standing two inches beyond the reaching hand, and does not look toward the bed; the widow's mark hangs where it hung, touched once before the kiln on Ember 1 and at no shelf, well, rack, road, basket, afternoon or dusk since, because none of these is an opening; the two rooms do not touch (T058/T079). In the small hours he turns out the file as a man lays instruments on a towel: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth from a person and no seventh invented, three near-full answers advanced and unpaid, the older intervals, nine stoppings as objects and not a rule with no tenth, three held changes on three separate places, the loft-sill sound on a fourth, the two shut-room tellings with no third, the told bell beside the heard, the told figure beside the paid, the carried body's pale line held on a place of its own and not laid across any of them, and the shelf's two gaps, the fold's crust and its gap, the pan's gone ring and the field's empty place on trays that do not touch, with no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause and no finger drawing the line (T061/T082, T060/T086, T065/T095, T097 held). Through the finger's-width door the river keeps its fifth note, through the floor the carried fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been with its payer unnamed for a hundred and eighty-eight days, and overhead the boards keep four nails, four and a knot the width of a thumb: three counts in three places that do not become one. Cold has come cheek, temple and the small bare joint at the wrist where the wool rides back and stopped as if it had reached the end of its own order; the afterdrop waits on the far side of a warming nobody in this house will perform. Close on one hundred and eighty-eight standing exact, complete and unspent in the dark of the wool, nothing joined, named, opened, called, spent or ended, his hand outside the wool going up an inch toward the note of water over water and coming down against the fold, and the count going forward into Day 189, Ember 10, the kiln month's first Account-day.
